Typical late-summer conditions—cool Pacific waters, limited afternoon solar heating under the marine inversion, and steady onshore winds—continue to suppress extreme warmth, consistent with historical August highs near 67 °F at downtown and airport stations. No recent model runs or observational shifts have introduced meaningful upside or downside risk, so market-implied odds remain tightly anchored to the official forecast envelope.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus centers on 32–34°C as the most probable maximum for Lucknow on August 21, 2026, reflecting ongoing monsoon conditions that favor moderate highs.** 

August climatology places typical daily maxima near 33°C (91°F) amid high humidity and frequent cloud cover. Recent model guidance and agency outlooks indicate thundery showers or isolated thunderstorms on the 21st, which limit solar heating and cap peaks around 32–34°C (roughly 90–93°F). Current forecasts from sources such as AccuWeather, BBC Weather, and timeanddate.com converge on this range, with some runs showing brief clearing that could allow 34–35°C if rain stays lighter than expected. 

Recent actual maxima have reached the mid-30s earlier in the month, yet persistent moisture and cloudiness have kept values from climbing higher. Market-implied odds therefore cluster tightly because traders weigh the strong likelihood of rain-cooled conditions against modest upside if steering patterns reduce precipitation. New model runs and official India Meteorological Department updates in the next 12–24 hours remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift probabilities within this narrow band.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader sentiment for Madrid’s August 21 peak temperature centers on model consensus for a 30–32 °C maximum under stable late-summer conditions.** Current ECMWF and GFS runs, together with AEMET guidance, indicate mostly sunny skies, light southerly or southwesterly flow, and limited moisture, keeping the daily high near the upper end of climatological norms for the date. Updated high-resolution runs and any AEMET afternoon advisory remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent high-resolution runs from AEMET and ECMWF place Madrid’s maximum temperature on August 22 near 33–34°C under mostly clear skies and light winds, following a mid-month cooldown from earlier peaks above 35°C. These conditions allow standard daytime insolation and boundary-layer heating without strong subsidence or advection that would push readings higher. Historical late-August climatology centers around 32°C, with values rarely exceeding 35°C absent persistent high pressure. The tight spread between the 33°C and 34°C outcomes reflects ensemble spread and minor differences in boundary-layer parameterization across models. Updated guidance and observational verification over the next 48 hours will likely resolve the narrow gap before the market closes.

Recent model updates have narrowed the spread by incorporating observed boundary-layer moisture and reduced insolation from overcast conditions, while the urban heat-island effect in central districts adds slight upward bias. Traders appear to weigh the balance between clearing skies that could push readings toward 36°C against more widespread rain that would cap the daily maximum closer to 34°C.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Active southwest monsoon conditions, with persistent cloud cover and scattered showers forecast for Metro Manila, are the main driver keeping trader consensus centered on 31–32°C peaks for August 22. Official PAGASA guidance projects a 32°C high amid 70% rain probability, while climatological August averages hover near 30–31°C; reduced insolation from monsoon clouds and evaporative cooling from rainfall limit daytime maxima. Minor forecast shifts in monsoon surge strength or brief clearing periods could tip outcomes toward 30°C or 33°C, reflecting the narrow uncertainty range reflected in the closely matched market-implied probabilities.
